## Decision record

<!-- agent-engineering:judgment:decisions-record:start -->
Load-bearing decisions this repository has already made. Architect reads this before proposing anything; re-deciding one of these is a regression, not a refactor.

**1. The kit is a workflow layer, never a second agent runtime.** The host owns models, isolated dispatch, permissions, edits and user interaction. OBSERVED `AGENTS.md:22`, `docs/DESIGN.md:5`.
**Rejected:** a model-host adapter system, and token or monetary accounting the host cannot measure. OBSERVED `docs/DESIGN.md:52`.

**2. Routing is behavioural, never lexical.** Five `--risk` flags each map deterministically to one expert; request keywords may only ADD a reviewer; an absent risk assessment is recorded and reported, never read as safety. OBSERVED `AGENTS.md:64`, implemented at `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:212`.
**Rejected:** keyword routing — the `oauth-login` eval case exists because "add OAuth login" matched no keyword and routed with no Security expert. OBSERVED `evals/cases.json:1`.

**3. Depth comes from lenses, not more roles.** A lens rides a role already running, costs no dispatch and carves out no ownership. Twenty ship; three named gaps stay in a backlog so a detected-but-unhandled domain fires `LENS UNAVAILABLE`. OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/references/lenses/_index.md:81`.
**Rejected:** a tenth specialist role, and per-stack Builders — splitting Builder would destroy the single-coherent-diff property verification depends on. OBSERVED `docs/DESIGN.md:59`.

**4. Method goes in roles, dated facts go in lenses.** A lens carries `verified:` and `review_after:` and declares itself `LENS STALE` rather than quoting a threshold nobody rechecked. OBSERVED `AGENTS.md:81`.

**5. Approval is two keys, and a reviewer verdict is not one of them.** `approve` refuses any role name as the approver, OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:771`; `phase --to build` refuses without a recorded approval, OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:724`; Builder re-checks before editing, OBSERVED `skills/ae-build/SKILL.md:55`.

**6. The report is rendered from the ledger, never recalled.** OBSERVED `AGENTS.md:78`, rendered at `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:940`.

**7. Enforcement is a read tier, with its limits shipped alongside the claim.** Every gate lives in `forge.mjs`, and whether `forge.mjs` ran was decided by prose — the instruction plane admitting or bypassing the control plane. A host hook now closes the narrowest useful part: no edit while a run still needs approval, no edit while a run is in `verify`. OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/scripts/guard.mjs:89`, declared at `hooks/hooks.json:1`, tier read at `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:295`, doctrine at `skills/ae-forge/references/team.md:136`.
**Rejected:** a blocking `Stop` hook — refusing to end a turn can strand a session with no way out, and the failure it would prevent is already visible in the report. OBSERVED `docs/DESIGN.md:53`.
**Never claimed:** that this is a sandbox. Hooks load in one host, from a file the model can edit, and a subagent may bypass them. The guard fails open on every malformed input, OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/scripts/guard.mjs:25`.

**8. The one cross-product-boundary artifact is versioned and asserted.** `analysis.json` carries `schema`; `team.json` declares `analysis_schema`; `lens-select.mjs` compares and reports `schema_mismatch`. OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/references/team.json:3` and `skills/ae-forge/scripts/lens-select.mjs:169`.
**Rejected:** continuing to read it with `?? []` and a bare `catch`. That turned a field rename into fewer lenses returned as a legitimate selection — the only fail-open path in a kit that is fail-closed everywhere else, and it was invisible.

**9. Two coupling styles, deliberately different.** Product boundaries are artifact-mediated; the six stage skills read `ae-forge/references/` as a sibling because they are one distribution unit with it. OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/references/team.md:116`.
**Rejected:** a "keep these in sync" instruction, which rots silently.

**10. Two user-facing routing surfaces; six dispatch targets.** OBSERVED `AGENTS.md:68`. The stage skills must read as unreachable outside a run, never as a second way to ask for work. Each stops rather than improvising when its sibling contract is missing.

**11. One event, one write.** `note` places the section its role owns when that section is still scaffolded, OBSERVED `skills/ae-forge/scripts/forge.mjs:723`. Previously the ledger and the artifact were two writes reconciled by a completion gap.
**Rejected:** deleting the `sections` gap. It is retained as a net; what changed is that forgetting can no longer trip it.

**12. The survey refuses to treat its own repository as a consumer.** `ae_self_hosted` gates the suite ignore rule, the untrack advice and the lock warning. OBSERVED `skills/ae-surveyor/scripts/lib.sh:183`.
**Why it matters:** the rule `**/skills/ae-*/` hides every uncommitted skill directory from `git status` in the kit's own tree, and the untrack advice would delete the product.

**13. Comment masking is line-based, not tokenised.** OBSERVED `skills/ae-surveyor/scripts/sense.mjs:95`.
**Rejected:** a character-level scanner. It must tokenise the language to tell a string quote from a quote inside a regex literal; this repository is full of the latter, and getting it wrong desynchronises the scanner and silently stops masking anything — which looks like it works. Masking less, predictably, beats masking more, unreliably.

**14. The suite runs in CI, on both platforms.** OBSERVED `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1`.
**Why both:** four of the eleven checks are shell scripts, and the runner resolves Git Bash by absolute path specifically to avoid the WSL shim — a path that is only exercised if Windows actually runs.
**Rejected:** an `npm ci` step. The suite is dependency-free by policy, so it would be decoration, and decoration in a gate file is how a gate stops being read.

**15. The generator stamps itself, and every copy of its version is asserted.** OBSERVED `skills/ae-surveyor/scripts/artifact-support.mjs:33`; five copies compared at `scripts/test-packaging.mjs:84`; drift detected at `skills/ae-surveyor/scripts/doctor.sh:203`.
**Why a fifth copy inside the skill:** a project install receives skill directories, not the repository root, so `kit.json` (OBSERVED `skills/ae-surveyor/references/kit.json:2`) is the only version an installed generator can cite.
**The failure it closes:** a survey could not say it predated a fix. The stamp recorded what was read — snapshot, input sha, commit — and never what read it, so an artifact written by an older kit was indistinguishable from a current one.

**16. Still open, and deliberately not fixed here.** Three findings from the 2026-09-22 review remain, each because it changes behaviour a user should choose rather than inherit: no failing-test-first evidence for `kind: bug`; `feature` acceptance carries `requires: []`; and neither `audit` nor `verify` scopes "the project's checks" to the components a diff touched. A fourth is smaller: `note` requires `--result` to exist, so an interrupted Builder leaves no contribution record at all.

## Notes

<!-- Human notes survive regeneration. Revalidate them when source changes. -->

### Self-hosting hazard (2026-09-22)

`ae-surveyor` stage 1 is unsafe against its own repository. `scaffold.sh`
appends `**/skills/ae-*/` to `.gitignore` on the premise that installed skills
are a dependency. In this repository `skills/` is the product. Already-tracked
files survive (git ignore does not untrack), but every **untracked** skill
directory disappears from `git status` — verified with `git check-ignore -v`,
which attributes `skills/ae-build/SKILL.md` to that pattern. `doctor.sh` then
reports the tracked copies as a warning and advises removing them from the git
index, which would delete the product.

The scaffolded `.gitignore` block was reverted immediately. The AGENTS.md
pointer block was kept, with a correction appended below its end marker.

This is a hazard, not a proven cause: the pattern is not in `HEAD`, so it did
not itself hide the currently-untracked directories.
